questions.prompt: Which gases cause acid rain? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides dissolve in rain to form sulfuric and nitric acids.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of acid rain formation in order.
steps: Fossil fuels are burned in power stations and vehicles
Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides are released
The gases dissolve in water droplets in clouds
Acid rain falls, sometimes far away
questions.explain: Burn → release → dissolve → acids form → acid rain.

questions.prompt: Clean, unpolluted rain has a pH of about…

feedback.1: Clean rain is slightly acidic because CO₂ dissolves in it.

questions.explain: Dissolved carbon dioxide makes clean rain slightly acidic, about pH 5.6.

questions.prompt: Why does acid rain damage marble monuments like the Taj Mahal?
options: Marble is calcium carbonate, which reacts with acids
questions.explain: Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide: the marble slowly dissolves.

questions.prompt: Would each action INCREASE or DECREASE acid rain?

items.label: Switching buses to CNG or electric
More old diesel vehicles on the road

questions.explain: Less burning of sulfur-containing fuels and fewer nitrogen oxides means less acid rain.

questions.text: The damage caused to marble by acid rain is sometimes called marble ___.
questions.explain: 'Marble cancer' describes the pitting and yellowing of marble.

questions.prompt: Why is acid rain described as a problem that 'crosses borders'?
options: Winds carry polluting gases far away, so rain can be acidic far from the source
It is caused by border fences
questions.explain: Pollution travels with the wind, so the damage may happen in another state or country.

questions.prompt: Match each effect of acid rain to what it harms.
questions.explain: Acid rain affects buildings, water life and plants.

questions.prompt: Describe TWO actions India took to protect the Taj Mahal from air pollution, and explain how each helps.
questions.modelAnswer: 1) The Taj Trapezium Zone made coal-based industries switch to cleaner fuels like natural gas or relocate, cutting sulfur dioxide emissions that form acid rain. 2) Restricting petrol and diesel vehicles near the monument reduces nitrogen oxides and soot around the marble.
rubric: One action (e.g. cleaner fuels / industries moved)
A second action (e.g. vehicle restrictions / multani mitti cleaning)
Explained how each reduces acid rain or damage
questions.explain: Real solutions combine science, law and community action.
